problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]?$

activity_context.topic_title: Computing the Singular Values of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Rectangular Matrix

examples.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$  

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & 1-\lambda  \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )^{2}-(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda ) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -1)(\lambda -2) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 & 12 \\ 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}13-\lambda  & 12 \\ 12 & 13-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (13-\lambda )(13-\lambda )-144 & =0 \\ 169-26\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-144 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-26\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$
